item.title: Abelardo Morell: The Universe Next Door — Thu Oct 22, 5:30 PM — Eskenazi Museum of Art at Indiana University
item.description: Hear from renowned photographer and educator Abelardo Morell about his art and career! 5:30-6:30 PM, Artist talk and Q&A, Martin Commons, second floor 6:30-7:00 PM, Enjoy Morell’s photographs in The Photographic Reflex, Featured Exhibition, first floor Abelardo Morell’s photographs reach through art history to one of the earliest predecessors of the medium, the camera obscura. In conjunction with the featured exhibition The Photographic Reflex: The Lee Marks and John C. DePrez Jr. Collection, the photographer will speak about his artistic practice and delve into his remarkable career. He has continually returned to the fundamental mechanics of light and vision, using them to transform ordinary rooms and landscapes into sites of quiet revelation. To make his most celebrated body of work, Morell darkens an entire room and leaves a single small opening in a window. Light passes through that aperture and projects an inverted image of the outside world onto the interior walls. City streets,

item.title: Sweet Sweetback's Baadasssss Song | The Long Revolution — Thu Oct 22, 7:00 PM — IU Cinema
item.description:
After saving a Black Panther from some racist cops, a Black sex worker goes on the run from “the man” with the help of the Black community and some disillusioned Hells Angels, soundtracked by original music from Earth, Wind, and Fire. Preserved in the Library of Congress' National Film Registry for its cultural, historical, and aesthetic significance, this Blaxploitation classic inspired everyone from Huey Newton to Spike Lee. [97 min; thriller, drama; English]

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Fri Oct 23 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Oct 23 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Fri Oct 23 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Fri Oct 23, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.

item.description: Chef Martin from B-town’s very own Osteria Rago might not have Italian heritage, but he’s definitely got Louisana roots. Chef Martin invites you to come explore oyster varieties and recipes including raw preparations with classic mignonette, Bienville style, and Rockefeller style. From shucking to baking, frying and more, there’s a lot of options and a lot to learn when it comes to these water creatures. item.title: HAYRAISER 5K Fun Run at The Goat Conspiracy Sanctuary — Sat Oct 24, 9:00 AM — The Goat Conspiracy Sanctuary
item.description:
Fall is in the air! Join us for a fun run through the fields of The Goat Conspiracy Sanctuary. Our second annual HAYRAISER 5k gives you the chance to get out in nature, meet our amazing goat and chicken residents, and help us fundraise for winter. Come out for a fun run/walk or run the course twice for a full 5K. The trail is 'off-road' through our 46-acre property in Brown County. - Check-in and gates open at 9:00 am - Race starts at 10:00 am - Includes self-guided visits with the goats and chickens - Registration $20, Kids 12 and under $10 (kids 2 and under are free) The PLANTED Bloomington food truck will be on site selling delicious plant-based fare from 10am-1pm. Contact info@thegoatconspiracy.org if you have any questions! Pavilion race start/end location, parking, and Planted food truck location are wheelchair accessible. The race course goes through the pastures and is not wheelchair accessible.
Source: Visit Bloomington

item.title: Full Moon Hike — Sat Oct 24, 7:00 PM — Olympic Pool parking lot
item.description:
Join a park naturalist for a guided night hike on the Salt Creek Trail! The Full Moon is the brightest night of the month, leading to interesting views along the creek. Learn about October’s full moon this year, the Hunter’s Moon. The Salt Creek Trail is rated very easy, but should be considered moderate in the dark. The trail has some minor slopes, a short stretch of lawn, and possible wet or icy spots depending on weather. Our route is about 2 miles total and will take about an hour to complete. Please do not bring pets on night hikes. Red flashlights are preferred for night vision and can be loaned to hikers on request.

item.title: Sourdough Bootcamp — Sun Oct 25, 1:00 PM — In the Kitchen
item.description:
Sourdough bootcamp with Madeleine is the class for sourdough newcomers. This class will give you a run down on all the sourdough tips and tricks you’ll need to become a master baker. Madeleine’s sourdough recipe is baked in a steamy oven, yielding a delightfully tender crust. It’s perfect for mix-ins like chocolate or cheddar, and better yet, it’s probably one of the easiest sourdough recipes you’ll ever find. She will discuss sourdough do’s and don’ts with an emphasis on creating and nurturing starter. There’s nothing quite like fresh bread, and Madeleine really does simplify the process. Hands on class with Madeleine. You leave with starter, dough and fresh bread! We encourage you to sign up for classes online. When you register online, you’ll also pay online. While we will accept walk-ins before class if capacity allows, registering ahead of time secures your spot and creates a more seamless class experience.

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Mon Oct 26 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Mon Oct 26 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment examines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Mon Oct 26 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers
